# New renderings and departures, iliad-048 (8.198–291)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| καί ῥα Ποσειδάωνα μέγαν θεὸν ἀντίον ηὔδα (8.200, whole-line speech introduction) | "and to Poseidon, great god, face to face she spoke:" | "and spoke to Poseidon, the great god, face to face:" | "mighty god", "great Poseidon"; μέγας θεός is translated, and ἀντίον ηὔδα keeps the table's "face to face" |
| ἀπτοεπές (Ἥρη ἀπτοεπές, 8.209) | "reckless-of-speech" | "reckless talker" | "boastful", "unbridled", "foolish"; rare, the first part is not securely understood, and the note says "reckless of speech" is only the traditional gloss |
| θοῷ ἀτάλαντος Ἄρηϊ (8.215) | "the equal of swift Ares" | "the equal of swift Ares" | "swift-footed" (ὠκύποδες is that), "fleet"; ἀτάλαντος Ἄρηϊ "the equal of Ares" as in the table, with θοῷ "swift" added |
| μεγακήτεϊ (νηῒ μελαίνῃ, 8.222) | "huge" | "huge" | "great-bellied", "deep-hulled", "monster-sized"; probably μέγα- + κῆτος "sea-monster", but the formation is not secure, and the note says so |
| κενεαυχής (κενεαυχέες, 8.230) | "empty-boasters" | "empty boasters" | "braggarts", "vain boasters", "idle"; κενός "empty" + αὐχέω "boast" |
| ἀγοράασθαι (ἃς … ἠγοράασθε, 8.230; with εὐχωλάς as object) | "proclaimed" | "proclaimed" | "held forth in the assembly" (the table's 2.337 rendering, which has no object); here the boasts are the object, so "proclaimed" |
| κρητῆρας ἐπιστεφέας οἴνοιο (8.232; departure from the Odyssey's `i` "bowls brimming with wine", 8.431) | "mixing-bowls brimming with wine" | "mixing-bowls brimming with wine" | "bowls" alone (the Odyssey's `i`), which drops κρητήρ; the Iliad table already has κρητήρ "mixing-bowl" |
| οὐδ’ ἑνὸς ἄξιοί εἰμεν Ἕκτορος (8.234) | "not even of one are we worthy, of Hector" | "we are not worth even one Hector" | "equal to Hector", "a match for"; the genitive of value with ἑνός in apposition to Ἕκτορος |
| ἄτῃ ἄασας (8.237) | "with this bewilderment bewildered" | "bewildered … with a bewilderment like this" | "blinded", "ruined", "struck with folly"; ἄτη is "bewilderment" in the table (1.412, 2.111), and the verb ἀάω takes the same root in English |
| ἐπὶ πᾶσι (βοῶν δημὸν καὶ μηρί’ ἔκηα, 8.240) | "upon all" | "upon every one" | "on every altar" (the noun is not in the Greek); δημός "fat", μηρία "thigh-pieces" as in the table |
| ἔρρων (ἐνθάδε ἔρρων, 8.239) | "coming here wretchedly" | "on my wretched way here" | "doomed", "accursed"; ἔρρω is "go with ill luck", not a prophecy of ruin |
| ἀλλὰ Ζεῦ τόδε πέρ μοι ἐπικρήηνον ἐέλδωρ· (8.242, whole-line prayer) | "But, Zeus, this at least for me fulfil, the wish:" | "But, Zeus, fulfil at least this wish for me:" | "grant", "accomplish"; ἐπικρήηνον "fulfil" and ἐέλδωρ "wish" as at 1.41 and 5.455 |
| ὣς φάτο, τὸν δὲ πατὴρ ὀλοφύρατο δάκρυ χέοντα (8.245, whole line) | "So he spoke, and him the father pitied, a tear shedding," | "So he spoke, and the Father grieved for him as he shed tears," | "wept over him"; ὀλοφύρομαι is "grieve for" in the table (8.33), "pity" avoided
| τελειότατον (αἰετόν, 8.247) | "most perfect" | "most perfect" | "surest", "most unfailing", "most accomplished"; τέλειος is "perfect, complete", and the note gives the usual explanation (the bird whose sign is surest to be fulfilled) |
| πανομφαῖος (πανομφαίῳ Ζηνί, 8.250) | "of every divine voice" | "the source of every divine voice" | "all-prophetic", "of all oracles", "author of omens"; πᾶν + ὀμφή, and ὀμφή is "the divine voice" in the table (2.41); the exact sense is not certain, and the note says so |
| εὔχομαι with infinitive (οὔ τις … εὔξατο … σχέμεν, 8.254) | "claimed" | "could claim" | "prayed" (it is a claim, not a prayer); the note says so |
| ἐναντίβιον (μαχέσασθαι, 8.255) | "head-on" | "head-on" | "face to face" (kept for ἀντίον ηὔδα), "in opposition" (ἀντιβίην, 3.277), "man to man"; ἐναντίβιον is "against (his) strength" |
| ὑπεξέφερεν σάκος (8.268) | "would draw his shield aside" | "would draw his shield aside" | "lift", "hold out", "bear off"; ὑπεκφέρω is "carry out from under"; the verbs of 8.268–272 are iterative and the English says "would" |
| πάϊς ὣς ὑπὸ μητέρα δύσκεν (8.271) | "like a child, under his mother would slip in" | "like a child to its mother, and slip in beside Ajax" | "run to his mother" alone, which drops ὑπό and the application to Ajax |
| Names (8.274–276) | Orsilochus, Ormenus, Ophelestes, Daetor, Chromius, Lycophontes, Amopaon (Polyaemon’s-son), Melanippus | same (Amopaon, son of Polyaemon) | "Daitor", "Chromios" and other transliterations; familiar Latinised English forms, Orsilochus as already shipped (iliad-032); patronymics rendered "Polyaemon’s-son" in `l`, "son of Polyaemon" in `i` |
| καί μιν πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπε (8.280, whole-line speech introduction; pattern of 6.381) | "and he stood beside him, going up, and addressed him with a word:" | "He went up and stood beside him and spoke to him:" | "and spoke a word to him", "said"; πρὸς … ἔειπε "addressed with a word" as in the table |
| φίλη κεφαλή (8.281, vocative) | "dear head" | "dear head" | "dear friend", "dear one", "dear fellow"; the head standing for the man is the idiom, and the note says so |
| φόως (αἴ κέν τι φόως Δαναοῖσι γένηαι, 8.282) | "a light" | "a light" | "salvation", "deliverance"; the note says the light is a figure for rescue |
| κομίσσατο (8.284) | "took care of" | "took care of" | "took in", "nursed", "looked after"; κομίζω "take care of" |
| ἐπίβησον (ἐϋκλείης ἐπίβησον, 8.285) | "cause to step upon good fame" | "bring … to good fame" | "set on the road to", "lead to"; causative aorist of ἐπιβαίνω with the genitive |
| πρεσβήϊον (8.289) | "a prize of precedence" | "a prize of honour" | "the place of honour", "gift of honour" alone; γέρας is "prize" / "prize of honour" in the table, so `l` takes "precedence" to keep πρεσβήϊον apart from γέρας; the word is built on πρέσβυς "elder" and means the honour due to rank |
| αὐτοῖσιν ὄχεσφιν (8.290) | "with the very chariot" | "with the chariot itself" | "chariot and all" (colloquial); "with their harness" |
| ὁμὸν λέχος εἰσαναβαίνοι (8.291) | "who might go up into the same bed with you" | "who would go up into the same bed with you" | "share your bed" alone, which loses εἰσαναβαίνω "go up into"; no euphemism, not bowdlerized |
| ὣς ἔφατ’ εὐχόμενος (8.198) | "So he spoke, declaring" | "So he declared aloud" | table has "praying"; here Hector has vaunted, not prayed, so "declaring" |
| Follows the table unchanged | | | πότνια Ἥρη "lady Hera", ὀχθήσας "greatly troubled / vexed", κρείων ἐνοσίχθων "the lord earth-shaker", εὐρύοπα Ζεύς "far-thundering Zeus / Zeus who thunders from afar", Κρονίων "the son of Cronus", ἐννοσίγαι’ εὐρυσθενές (as at 7.455), πῦρ κηλέον "blazing fire", νῆας ἐΐσας "well-balanced ships", ὑπερμενής "exceeding-strong / of surpassing strength", νηῒ πολυκλήϊδι "a ship of many thwarts", χθονὶ πουλυβοτείρῃ "the much-nourishing earth / the earth that feeds so many", παλίντονα τόξα "back-stretched / recurved bow", ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν "lord of men", αἰγίοχος "aegis-bearing", ἐϋκτίμενον πτολίεθρον "well-built citadel", ἀτάλαντος Ἐνυαλίῳ ἀνδρειφόντῃ "the equal of Enyalius, killer of men" |
